subject: Release pulse: cadence + risk ownership
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Release pulse: cadence + risk ownership

Hi team,

Attaching a compact pulse ahead of the QBR prep this week — primary goal is to surface the top delivery risks that would change our launch window and get owners on record for mitigations. Attachment: release_velocity_snapshot.xlsx (snapshot of sprint burn + scope changes).

Key points:
- Velocity: Core model serving work is ~72% on-track vs. plan; decoder optimizations slipped ~2 sprints due to kernel tuning regressions.
- Blockers:
  * infra perf regression on 8-bit quantized weights (affects latency SLO on Dedicated) — reproducible locally, failing perf gate in nightly tests.
  * end-to-end e2e tests show intermittent KV cache eviction at sequence lengths > 2048 (low frequency but high impact).
- Launch timeline: nominal target 2027-07-15 for v1 GA; risk of moving by 2–3 weeks if perf regressions persist.
- Gate asks for QBR: concrete thresholds for latency P95 (<= 150ms on test rig) and regression-free nightly for 3 consecutive days, or scope-down plan.

Requests / next steps:
1) Irene — can you confirm infra debug owner and ETA for a reproducer + perf log?
2) Marcus — propose a scope reduction candidate set we can accept at readout if regressions persist.
3) Vivek — need guidance on whether leadership accepts a ~2-week contingency or we prepare a formal canary and rollback plan.

I can host a 30-min standup at 11:30 if that helps align.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: release_velocity_snapshot.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Release pulse: cadence + risk ownership

Thanks Marissa — quick update from infra.

Summary: the perf regression is isolated to the new quantization kernel we merged last sprint. Reproducer: running the nightly perf harness with batch size 1 and sequence profile A triggers the higher memory traffic pattern; see attached perf_log.txt for the failing trace.

Action items assigned:
- Owner: Irene Choi (infra) + Diego Fernandez (runtime) — we have an initial debug plan to A/B the kernel and run a reduced-precision fallback on the canary pool by tomorrow EOD.
- ETA: tentative hotfix branch by 2027-06-09 18:00 PT for canary validation; if that fails, we will auto-fallback to the previous kernel for Dedicated.

Notes: KV cache eviction looks orthogonal but may amplify tail latency; I've asked SRE to increase log sampling rate for sequences > 2048 and will drop a short findings note to the shared Drive link.

On the scope question: if we must keep timeline, we should scope down non-critical telemetry features (see suggested cut in lagging_issues.pdf). That preserves core serving and API parity.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Release pulse: cadence + risk ownership

Thanks — read this and sketched a couple of options.

Proposal (if perf hotfix is delayed beyond 2 business days):
- Option A (preferred): Scope down v1 to remove advanced telemetry (non-blocking; rollout in v1.1). This reduces end-to-end surface area we need to validate and keeps GA date. See attached lagging_issues.pdf for items.
- Option B (conservative): Move GA by 2 weeks to 2027-07-29 and use the extra cycle for stress-testing, extended canary, and a targeted benchmark sweep.

Gate criteria I recommend for QBR decision:
1) Performance: P95 latency <= 150ms on Dedicated with the canary kernel OR deterministic fallback path validated on canary.
2) Reliability: No KV-cache eviction events >= 1/min on canary over a 72-hour window.
3) Observability: Telemetry required for rollback decisions is present (trace IDs + token-level cost).

If leadership prefers not to accept a schedule slip, Option A is the operationally safer path. Posting a draft decision brief to Drive: https://drive.google.com/example-release-pulse and linking SUP-2029 for the telemetry cards.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Release pulse: cadence + risk ownership

Good work surfacing this. Quick leadership view and decision path:

- We will prioritize keeping GA date but only if Option A (scope reduction) is feasible with a clear rollback path. The business impact of slipping GA is material for a set of enterprise customers (HorizonPay included).
- Immediate asks:
  1) Marcus — finalize the scope-down list and call out any customer-impacting regressions by EOD 2027-06-08.
  2) Irene — validate the fallback kernel on canary by tomorrow morning; if it fails, we trigger the conservative path (Option B) and update customers via CS.

I approve preparing the Option A readout as the default plan for QBR; we will present both options and ask execs to endorse the fallback if needed. Marcus/Irene — reply "ACK" with your confirmation so I can include your owners in the QBR pack.
